finding.affected_use: F12 writes g_T^*(R^q f_* F|_U) and g_T^* F with one symbol for pullbacks from U and from X. These sheaves have different base spaces.
finding.reason: Name h:T->U and g_T:X_T->X separately and replace only the left pullback by h^*. The upper-semicontinuity proof via finite free matrices is unaffected; no Statement change is required.
finding.exact_snippet: [F12] Cohomology and base change (used only in the comparison of 1.10): for the family of the statement, a point $s\in S$ and $q\ge0$, the cohomology and base-change map is the $\kappa(s)$-linear map $\varphi^q_s:(R^qf_*\mathcal F)(s)\to H^q(X_s,\mathcal F_s)$ out of the fibre of the higher direct image sheaf ([[def-base-change-map-cohomology]], [[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]], [[def-fibre-of-module-at-point]], [[def-pullback-module-ringed-spaces]], [[def-residue-field-scheme-point]]). If $\varphi^q_s$ and $\varphi^{q-1}_s$ are surjective (the second condition being automatic for $q=0$), then $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ is locally free of finite rank in a neighbourhood of $s$, and there is an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that for every morphism $T\to U$ the base-change map $g_T^*(R^qf_*\mathcal F|_U)\to R^qf_{T*}(g_T^*\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_T$-modules; for $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ with $u\in U$ the left side has global sections the fibre $(R^qf_*\mathcal F)(u)$, by the affine localisation of higher direct images and the pullback formula for associated sheaves, and the right side has global sections $H^q(X_u,\mathcal F_u)$, so the fibre of the finite locally free sheaf $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ at $u$ is identified with $H^q(X_u,\mathcal F_u)$ and its dimension is the rank. ([[thm-cohomology-and-base-change]], [[lem-higher-direct-image-affine-localization]], [[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]], [[thm-affine-quasi-coherent-equivalence]], [[def-associated-sheaf-module-affine-scheme]], [[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]], [[def-base-change-morphism-schemes]], [[lem-fibre-product-open-restriction]])

downstream_reviews.exact_snippet: [F12] Cohomology and base change (used only in the comparison of 1.10): for the family of the statement, a point $s\in S$ and $q\ge0$, the cohomology and base-change map is the $\kappa(s)$-linear map $\varphi^q_s:(R^qf_*\mathcal F)(s)\to H^q(X_s,\mathcal F_s)$ out of the fibre of the higher direct image sheaf ([[def-base-change-map-cohomology]], [[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]], [[def-fibre-of-module-at-point]], [[def-pullback-module-ringed-spaces]], [[def-residue-field-scheme-point]]). If $\varphi^q_s$ and $\varphi^{q-1}_s$ are surjective (the second condition being automatic for $q=0$), then $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ is locally free of finite rank in a neighbourhood of $s$, and there is an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that for every morphism $T\to U$ the base-change map $g_T^*(R^qf_*\mathcal F|_U)\to R^qf_{T*}(g_T^*\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_T$-modules; for $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ with $u\in U$ the left side has global sections the fibre $(R^qf_*\mathcal F)(u)$, by the affine localisation of higher direct images and the pullback formula for associated sheaves, and the right side has global sections $H^q(X_u,\mathcal F_u)$, so the fibre of the finite locally free sheaf $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ at $u$ is identified with $H^q(X_u,\mathcal F_u)$ and its dimension is the rank.
